**Answer: c = 2**

This is ISL 2015 A8. The known result is that for every aquaesulian function, the values f(r) + f(−r) take at most two distinct rational values, so c = 2 works. The official solution shows that f(r) + f(−r) equals 0 for all rational r except possibly one fixed value, so at most two values occur. The identity f(x) = x is aquaesulian and gives only the value 0, so one value is not enough to force c = 2. Exhibiting an aquaesulian function with two distinct values of f(r) + f(−r) shows that c = 2 is sharp. I have not re-derived the full proof here, so this answer relies on the known result rather than a complete argument.

ANSWER: 2
